findings.title: get_cli_string produces an injectable shell command
findings.description: The function inserts path, action, key, quote, and value directly into a shell command string. Double-quoting values containing spaces does not protect against shell expansion, embedded double quotes, or command substitutions. A caller that executes the returned string through a shell can execute attacker-controlled commands.
findings.suggestion: Return an argument list for subprocess calls. If a shell string is required, quote every argument with a platform-appropriate quoting function.

findings.title: set_key accepts keys that can inject additional .env entries
findings.description: key_to_set is inserted directly into line_out. A key containing a newline can add arbitrary assignments to the file, which may subsequently be loaded into an application's or dotenv run's environment. The CLI exposes this behavior through its set command.
findings.suggestion: Reject keys containing line breaks and other invalid key characters before constructing the assignment.

findings.title: Symlink protection is subject to a filesystem race
findings.description: rewrite opens the source path before checking it with lstat, then later replaces the path by name. Another process can change that path between these operations, defeating the intended no-follow behavior or replacing a different file than the one read.
findings.suggestion: Use no-follow file-opening primitives where available, verify file identity with fstat, and document or otherwise mitigate the remaining atomic-replacement race.

findings.title: dotenv set prints the value it was asked to store
findings.description: On success, the set command echoes key=value, including passwords or tokens. This can expose secrets in CI logs and captured command output even when the .env file is protected.
findings.suggestion: Print a confirmation that omits the value, or provide an explicit option for displaying it.

findings.title: Concurrent .env updates can silently overwrite one another
findings.description: rewrite copies the existing file to a temporary file and replaces the original without locking or checking whether it changed during the copy. Two concurrent set_key or unset_key calls can each succeed while one discards the other's update.
findings.suggestion: Coordinate writers with a file lock or detect changes and retry before replacement.

findings.title: The parser reads the entire input into memory
findings.description: Reader calls stream.read() without a size bound. Loading a very large .env file or a continuously written FIFO can consume unbounded memory before parsing begins.
findings.suggestion: Parse incrementally or enforce a configurable input-size limit, particularly for FIFO and externally supplied streams.

findings.title: Variable expansion repeatedly copies the environment
findings.description: For each assignment, resolve_variables builds a new dictionary containing os.environ and all previously resolved assignments. Parsing many entries therefore incurs quadratic copying in the number of .env keys.
findings.suggestion: Use a layered mapping or another lookup strategy that preserves override precedence without copying all earlier values for each key.

findings.title: run_command docstring incorrectly says it never returns
findings.description: The docstring says the current process is replaced and the function does not return. On Windows, the implementation starts a subprocess, waits for it, and exits with its status; that is materially different process and signal behavior.
findings.suggestion: Document the Unix exec and Windows subprocess paths separately.

findings.title: load_dotenv docstring overstates its return value
findings.description: The docstring says True means at least one environment variable is set. DotEnv.set_as_environment_variables also returns True when the file has a parsed key but no assignment is made, such as a key without a value or an existing variable with override=False.
findings.suggestion: Describe True as indicating that at least one key was parsed, or change the implementation to track actual assignments.

findings.title: dotenv_values stream documentation is narrower than the API
findings.description: The stream parameter is documented as a StringIO object, but the implementation accepts general text streams, including open files, as the README and tests demonstrate.
findings.suggestion: Describe stream as an IO[str] text stream.

findings.title: Parameterized list test checks the built-in format instead of output_format
findings.description: The condition `if format is not None` is always true because format refers to Python's built-in function. For the None parameter case, the test appends None as a CLI argument instead of exercising the default output format.
findings.suggestion: Change the condition to `if output_format is not None`.

findings.title: CLI subprocess tests depend on Unix printenv
findings.description: Several run tests invoke printenv without a Windows skip or a portable substitute. They fail on systems that do not provide that external command, independently of dotenv's behavior.
findings.suggestion: Use sys.executable with a short Python command to inspect the environment, or skip these cases when printenv is unavailable.

findings.title: IPython tests leave the process working directory changed
findings.description: The tests call os.chdir(tmp_path) without restoring the original directory. Later tests can run from a deleted temporary directory and behave differently depending on execution order.
findings.suggestion: Use monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path), which restores the working directory after each test.

findings.title: find_dotenv tests leave the process working directory changed
findings.description: The find_dotenv tests call os.chdir(leaf) without restoring it. When the temporary directory is removed, subsequent tests can inherit a nonexistent working directory.
findings.suggestion: Use the monkeypatch.chdir fixture in each test that changes directories.

findings.title: Shell-command tests omit hostile arguments
findings.description: The get_cli_string tests cover ordinary values and spaces but not shell metacharacters, command substitution, embedded quotes, or hostile paths. They therefore do not detect the command-injection behavior in this public helper.
findings.suggestion: Add cases for every interpolated argument containing shell syntax and assert safe execution or a safely quoted result.

findings.title: Mutation tests do not cover invalid or multiline keys
findings.description: The set_key tests exercise values and existing-file behavior but do not test keys containing newlines or invalid syntax. This leaves the .env-entry injection path untested.
findings.suggestion: Add API and CLI tests that reject invalid keys and verify that the file remains unchanged.

findings.title: Contributor instructions invoke the wrong formatter command
findings.description: `uv format .` is not the Ruff formatter command used by this project. Following the listed test workflow does not run the configured formatter.
findings.suggestion: Use `uv run ruff format .`, or `uvx ruff format .` if Ruff is not installed in the environment.

findings.title: Published contributor instructions invoke the wrong formatter command
findings.description: `uv format .` does not invoke the Ruff formatter configured in .pre-commit-config.yaml.
findings.suggestion: Replace it with `uv run ruff format .` and keep this published copy synchronized with CONTRIBUTING.md.

findings.title: Pre-commit installation command names a nonexistent executable
findings.description: The installed package's executable is `pre-commit`, but the guide tells contributors to run `uv run precommit install`.
findings.suggestion: Use `uv run pre-commit install`.

findings.title: Published pre-commit command names a nonexistent executable
findings.description: The guide uses `uv run precommit install`, while the dependency provides the `pre-commit` executable.
findings.suggestion: Use `uv run pre-commit install`.

findings.title: MkDocs link has no destination
findings.description: The text uses `[mkdocs]()` rather than linking to a destination, so the contributor guide provides a broken reference.
findings.suggestion: Link to the MkDocs documentation or remove the empty link syntax.

findings.title: Published MkDocs link has no destination
findings.description: The published guide also uses `[mkdocs]()`, leaving its documentation-tool reference without a destination.
findings.suggestion: Provide a URL for MkDocs or render the name as plain text.

findings.title: Variable expansion is described as general POSIX expansion
findings.description: The README says python-dotenv can interpolate variables using POSIX variable expansion. The regex in variables.py supports only `${name}` and `${name:-default}`; other POSIX forms such as `$name` and `${name:=default}` are not expanded.
findings.suggestion: Describe the supported forms explicitly rather than implying general POSIX expansion.

findings.title: Published variable-expansion description overstates supported syntax
findings.description: The published copy describes POSIX variable expansion, while variables.py recognizes only `${name}` and `${name:-default}`.
findings.suggestion: List the supported forms and state that other shell expansion syntax is not implemented.

findings.title: Version 1.0.0 comparison omits version 0.21.1
findings.description: The [1.0.0] link compares v0.21.0 to v1.0.0 even though this changelog lists v0.21.1 as the immediately preceding release. The comparison includes unrelated changes from that earlier patch release.
findings.suggestion: Compare v0.21.1 to v1.0.0.

findings.title: Published 1.0.0 comparison omits version 0.21.1
findings.description: The [1.0.0] comparison starts at v0.21.0, not the preceding v0.21.1 release shown in this changelog.
findings.suggestion: Change the link to compare v0.21.1 to v1.0.0.

findings.title: Unused MkDocs include-markdown plugin is installed
findings.description: mkdocs-include-markdown-plugin is listed as a documentation dependency, but mkdocs.yml does not enable its plugin and the provided documentation does not use its include syntax.
findings.suggestion: Remove the dependency unless documentation includes are planned and configured.

findings.title: Developer dependencies have no reproducible version bounds
findings.description: Most developer tools, including pytest, tox, Ruff, build, and pre-commit, have no upper bound or pinned version, and no lock file is provided. Fresh contributor installs can pick up incompatible releases and produce results different from CI or earlier installs.
findings.suggestion: Commit a development lock file or pin compatible tool versions and update them deliberately.

findings.title: bumpversion has no visible use in the supplied project configuration
findings.description: bumpversion is installed for development, but the provided configuration, scripts, and contribution instructions contain no version-bump command or configuration for it.
findings.suggestion: Remove it if version bumps are handled another way, or document and configure its intended workflow.

findings.title: Documentation dependencies are not locked
findings.description: The documentation requirements use open-ended minimum versions with no lock file. A fresh installation may render or build the site differently after upstream releases.
findings.suggestion: Lock documentation-tool versions for reproducible builds, while updating the lock regularly.
